parts.html: Creating a 3D visualization of a building facade involves several stages, each with its own features, possible revisions, and cost:

blocks.text: 1. Collection and analysis of the technical assignment (brief)

parts.html: At this stage, drawings, plans, reference materials, and examples are provided to help form a clear understanding of the project.

items: Cost: Usually included in the overall project price. However, if the brief requires significant development, an additional fee may apply (approximately €50–125).
Revisions: No design revisions are made at this stage — only clarifications of details.

parts.html: A three-dimensional model of the building facade is developed based on drawings and plans.

items: Cost: €200–375 (depending on the complexity and facade area).
Revisions: Basic shape adjustments are free. Major changes that require reworking the model are subject to an additional fee (around €50 per revision).

parts.html: Materials and textures (e.g., stone, brick, glass) are applied to the model according to the technical brief.

items: Cost: €125–250, depending on the number of textures and material complexity.
Revisions: 1–2 rounds of adjustments (e.g., color changes) are included for free. Full texture replacements are charged additionally (around €40 per round).

parts.html: Lighting and the building’s surroundings are modeled to create a realistic visualization.

items: Cost: €75–200, depending on complexity.
Revisions: One round of lighting adjustments is included; additional changes are charged at €25 per revision.

parts.html: A basic render is produced for preliminary review.

items: Cost: Usually included in the project price.
Revisions: Minor adjustments to the camera angle are free. More significant changes cost €25–50.

parts.html: After the draft render is approved, a high-quality final visualization is created.

items: Cost: €250–500 per view.
Revisions: No edits are included at this stage, as changes require re-rendering (€75–125 depending on complexity).

parts.html: Additional adjustments not specified in the initial brief.

items: Cost: Evaluated individually (€40–125 per change).
Revisions: Billed separately if not included in the original agreement.

parts.html: Includes modeling and visualization of elements surrounding the facade (trees, pathways, lighting).
Cost:

items: Basic environment: €125–250
Detailed landscape: €250–625

parts.html: Revisions: One round of adjustments to the placement of key elements is included for free. Major changes cost €50–100 per round.
Includes modeling of buildings, landscaping elements, and environment for adjacent lots.

items: Second lot: Basic modeling — €200–375. If detailed environment and landscaping are required, add €250–500. Final render (per view) — €250–500.
Third lot: Pricing is the same as for the second lot.

parts.html: Revisions:

items: One round of minor adjustments (e.g., object positioning) is free.
Major changes (e.g., replacing design elements) are charged separately — €50–125 per lot.

parts.html: At this stage, a unique facade or site design concept is developed. The service includes an analysis of architectural trends, creation of several conceptual facade sketches, development of an overall style, and selection of materials and key forms. It’s ideal for clients who don't yet have a clear technical brief but want to see a creative solution.
Process:
1. Client preference analysis (questionnaire, discussion of ideas and references)
2. Creation of several conceptual facade sketches (2–3 options)
3. Refinement of the selected concept and its development into a 3D model
Cost:

items: Facade concept development: €375–750 per facade
Advanced concept (including lot and detailed surroundings): €500–1250

parts.html: Revisions:

items: Included: 1–2 rounds of revisions for the selected concept
Extra: Additional concept options or major redesigns — from €125 per round

parts.html: Deliverables: After approval, the client receives the final 3D model and low-resolution renders for initial discussion.

Example Use Case: This service is ideal for clients who haven't yet decided on a specific facade style or want to explore modern and unique solutions. Once the concept is approved, a full 3D visualization is created based on it.

blocks.text: 11. Visualization of an Existing Project with Environmental Integration

parts.html: This service includes 3D visualization of an already developed building project (based on provided drawings or plans), with the goal of placing it within a realistic or simulated environment. The purpose is to demonstrate how the design will look within its surrounding context — including landscape, neighboring structures, and natural elements.
Workflow
1. Creation of a 3D model of the building from provided documentation
2. Development of the environment (landscape, roads, neighboring plots, trees, etc.)
3. Integration of the building into the scene and lighting setup
4. Final rendering from the selected camera angles
Pricing
Modeling of the building: €250–500 (depending on detail and complexity)
Environmental modeling:

items: Basic environment (lawn, a few trees, simple elements): €125–250
Detailed landscaping and context: €250–750

parts.html: Final rendering: €250–500 per angle
Revisions
✅ Included: 1 round of adjustments for environment integration (e.g., object placement, minor landscaping edits)
🔁 Additional costs:

items: Major modifications to the building model: €75–125
Redesign of the environment or adding new elements: €50–125

parts.html: Deliverables

items: High-resolution final renders from selected angles
Draft renders for client approval if needed

parts.html: Example Use Case: This service is ideal for architects who need to demonstrate how a completed project will integrate into a specific location — whether for investor presentations, marketing purposes, or regulatory approvals.
The final cost will depend on the complexity of the project, the required level of detail, and the number of revisions.
If the project includes a unified concept for all areas, part of the work can be optimized, which may reduce the total cost.
